explicit_propositions.text: North Carolina Democratic Governor Roy Cooper vetoed Senate Bill 360.
Senate Bill 360 aimed to prohibit collusive settlements involving the legislature as a defendant without its consent.
The bill required that when the General Assembly intervenes in a lawsuit, both the legislature and other defendants must be party to any settlement.
Governor Cooper claimed the bill was unconstitutional and unwise.
The attorney general, Josh Stein, settled a lawsuit with the Board of Elections without informing Republican defendants.
Purdue University developed a paint that reflects 98.1% of solar radiation and cools surfaces below ambient temperature.
Mark Elias, a lawyer linked to the Redistricting Project and Eric Holder, was involved in the settlement agreement.
The settlement altered state law during an ongoing election process.
McClatchy’s headline misrepresented the bill as transferring executive power to the legislature.
Roy Cooper previously sued to retain control of the North Carolina Board of Elections.
